title: [9/12/2025] - Average House Price across three countries in 1997 and 2014
prompt: The graph below shows the average house prices in 3 countries between the years 1997-2014. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the changes in average house prices in three different countries over a 17-year period from 1997 to 2014.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, all three countries experienced an upward trend in average housing costs throughout the period shown. Notably, Country A consistently maintained the highest property prices for the majority of the timeframe, particularly from 2001 onwards.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with Country A, house prices stood at $150,000 in 1997. The figures then witnessed a dramatic surge, reaching a peak of approximately $530,000 in 2003, before declining to around $460,000 by 2006. Following this dip, prices rose sharply once more, hitting another peak of $615,000 in 2012, before stabilizing at roughly $620,000 at the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the other two countries, in 1997, Country B's average house price was $130,000, while Country C recorded a lower figure of $100,000. Country B saw its values climb to $375,000 in 2005, then experienced a notable drop to $270,000 in 2008. Subsequently, the prices recovered and peaked at $520,000 in 2012, before declining slightly to finish at $490,000 in 2014. A similar pattern was observed in Country C, whose figures increased steadily to $240,000 in 2007, but then plummeted significantly to $150,000 in 2008. However, they recovered thereafter, ending the period at $280,000.
